body.intro: Pyra is a Solana-based fintech platform that pairs a traditional banking experience — cards, virtual accounts, payments — with on-chain yield and collateralised credit. Brought on as the team's first outside hire, I took ownership of rebuilding the mobile app from the ground up.
body.built: I built and owned the core surfaces end to end: onboarding and KYC, biometric and passkey authentication, card management, virtual accounts, payments, and the portfolio and credit flows — wiring the React Native app to Solana through the Pyra Labs SDK and an embedded Privy wallet.
body.scale: Alongside feature work I owned performance optimisation and release management — EAS builds, OTA updates and store submissions. Over ten months the platform scaled from roughly $50K to more than $4.8M in volume.

body.intro: iOvaro is a cross-platform invoicing app for freelancers and small businesses: build professional invoices and estimates from a multi-step editor, export them as branded PDFs, and get paid online. I built it from the ground up as a contractor at Applica, owning the mobile architecture end to end.
body.built: I implemented the full document builder across four PDF templates, customer management and multi-currency support, then wired up the money side: Stripe Connect so users get paid via generated payment links, and RevenueCat for in-app subscriptions. Auth, security and data ran on Firebase — social and email sign-in, an OTP flow, passcode plus biometric lock, Firestore and Cloud Functions.
body.delivery: Beyond features I owned the architecture decisions, release management and both the App Store and Play Store submissions, and mentored a junior developer through code reviews and pair programming. The product went from concept to a production release in roughly three months.

body.intro: Pocket Caddie is an AI-powered golf analytics app. Players record their golf swings on their phone, upload the clips for analysis by backend AI models, and get performance feedback they can track over time. I built the mobile experience from the ground up as a contractor at Applica.
body.built: I built the full video pipeline around Vision Camera — swing capture, frame-accurate trimming with a custom range slider, thumbnail generation and resumable uploads to Firebase Storage — feeding the clips to Cloud Functions and the AI analysis backend. On top of it I built the swing-review, comparison and progress-tracking screens with animated charts and circular score gauges.
body.delivery: Beyond feature work I owned architecture decisions, release management and both the App Store and Play Store submissions, and mentored a junior developer through code reviews and pair programming. The result was a complete, working prototype delivered to the client end to end — from swing capture and trimming through to video upload for AI analysis.

body.intro: Alex Motors is a working one-man garage on the Donegal–Derry border. The site is its entire digital presence: a single cinematic page that has to earn a local customer's trust in one scroll — services, customer reviews, an FAQ and instant ways to get in touch. I owned everything solo: concept and art direction, front end, edge backend, testing and CI.
body.built: The visual idea is a neon garage sign at night. The logo flickers on over a brick wall that runs seamlessly beneath all five full-screen scenes, and paging between them is owned entirely by native CSS scroll snap — after prototyping a JS wheel-paging layer I removed it completely, having proven that the browser's directional snapping does the job with zero scroll-hijacking bugs. Everything is built accessibility-first: ARIA tablists with roving tabindex, live regions, inert crossfade decks that keep all content crawlable, and every animation gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
body.delivery: The site ships as a Cloudflare Worker: static assets at the edge plus a POST /api/contact endpoint that validates against the same shared contract as the browser form, filters bots with a honeypot, and hand-builds an RFC 5322 email for Cloudflare Email Routing. Three languages — English, Irish and Russian — run on a custom typed dictionary instead of an i18n library, including a unicode-range font fallback that serves a heavier Cyrillic cut so Russian display text matches the Latin face optically. Quality is enforced by Vitest unit tests, a Playwright smoke suite against the real dev server, and GitHub Actions CI on every PR.

About.title: Who I am & how I got here
About.bio: I'm a Senior React Native developer focused on cross-platform mobile delivery, performance and product scaling — most recently across FinTech and HealthTech. I care about apps that feel fast and truly native, and I lean on AI-assisted tooling to ship production-quality work quickly.

pyra.blurb: Joined a Web3 FinTech card product as the first external engineer and led the iOS/Android rebuild while volume scaled from $50K to $4.8M+ over 10 months — shipping 40+ screens and cutting cold-start time by ~60%.

applica.blurb: Delivered two production apps end to end — a cross-platform invoicing product and an AI-powered golf analytics app — owning architecture, implementation and store releases, and mentored a junior developer.

freelance.blurb: Modernised a legacy React Native dating app across mobile and a Node.js/MongoDB backend, cutting screen load times by ~50% and crash rates by ~70% while lifting registration completion.

cloudfactory.blurb: Built mobile and web for a large-scale FinTech investment platform serving 200K+ users, with real-time portfolio management and trade-execution flows.

decision-mapper.blurb: Delivered 4+ cross-platform apps across education, dating and social domains, designing scalable mobile and backend architecture from build to release.

kport.blurb: Built 10+ Drupal websites end to end — backend configuration through responsive frontend — and shipped SEO improvements that grew organic visibility.

graduation.blurb: The maths grounding behind the engineering — still shapes how I break problems down.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: This site is a personal portfolio. It sets no cookies, runs no analytics or third-party trackers, and builds no profile of the people who visit it. The only place it collects anything is the contact form — and only what you type there.

form.title: The contact form
form.body: When you send a message, the name, email and message you enter are delivered straight to my inbox as an email so I can reply. They aren't stored in a database, sold, or shared with anyone else, and I use them only to respond to you. Ask me any time and I'll delete your message.

spam.title: Spam protection
spam.body: To stop the form being abused, submissions are checked by Cloudflare Turnstile — a privacy-preserving alternative to CAPTCHA. To tell humans from bots, Cloudflare processes limited technical data (such as your IP address); it doesn't use it to track you across sites. The details are in Cloudflare's

hosting.title: Hosting
hosting.body: The site is served from Cloudflare's global edge network. To deliver and protect it, Cloudflare processes standard request metadata such as your IP address and browser type. Nothing is retained by me.
